method: Ground distance to a depression angle theta is h / tan(theta), with h in metres and theta in degrees. The beam centre uses the downtilt; the near edge uses the downtilt plus half the vertical beamwidth and the far edge uses the downtilt minus half of it, so there is no far ground edge when the upper half-power edge is at or above the horizon. The footprint is the far edge minus the near edge, the slant range is h / sin(theta), and the path width at the aim point is twice the centre distance times tan of half the horizontal beamwidth. The radio horizon is 4.12 x sqrt(h) km and is used only to flag a footprint that curvature would shorten. Inputs are metres or feet (decimal comma accepted), heights 1-300 m (3.3-984 ft), downtilt 1-45 degrees, vertical beamwidth 2-60 degrees and horizontal beamwidth 10-120 degrees. The model assumes flat ground with no terrain, structures or vegetation, a symmetric main beam, and no earth curvature in the footprint distances; it does not account for side lobes, antenna gain beyond the half-power width, or RF exposure limits.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Antenna (radio): a directional antenna concentrates power in a main beam whose half-power beamwidth is the angular width where radiated power falls to half its peak.
